xmldoc.short_description: Read a PhysioNet WFDB record into the neutral struct.

param_input_item.param_description: the record, with or without its .hea extension.

for 'Signals', the signals to keep, by label (a char or a cellstr) or by index, in the order asked (by default every signal); for 'Annotations', the annotation file: 'auto' (the default) reads name.atr when present and skips it when absent, an extension such as 'qrs' reads name.qrs, a path reads that file, and false reads none.
a logical: 'Physical' whether to return each signal in physical units (false by default, so the raw ADC integers are returned), 'Data' whether to read the samples (true by default).

param_output_item.param_description: the neutral struct: the header, one entry per signal with its samples at its own rate, and the annotations.

description.p: The one reader of the PhysioNet WFDB record format. It returns a domain-free struct: nothing in it assumes leads, beats, sleep events or any other interpretation.

A record is a text header (name.hea) that describes the signals, followed by one or more binary signal files it names. A stored integer becomes a physical value by physical = (raw - baseline) / gain. By default the samples are the raw ADC integers the file holds, so a read followed by wfdb.write is lossless; the gain, baseline and unit of every signal are on r, so physical units are one step away, and 'Physical', true applies the conversion at the read. The samples of all signals are interleaved frame by frame in the signal file and de-interleaved in one pass, because a long record holds tens of millions of samples.

The returned struct has the fields kind ('wfdb.record'), name, path, rate (the base sampling frequency), counterFrequency, baseCounter, declaredFrames, startTime, startTimeKnown, startDate, comments, multiSegment, multiFrequency, segments, signals (a struct array with file, format, spf, offset, skew, gain, baseline, unit, adcres, adczero, initial, checksum, blocksize, description, label, rate and data) and annotations (sample, time, code, symbol, num, subtype, chan and aux).

A signal recorded at a slower rate carries more than one sample per frame (spf), and a record whose signals have different rates sets multiFrequency. A record whose header names segments instead of signals sets multiSegment and the segments are stitched into one signal array.

xmldoc.bibliography: Goldberger et al., PhysioBank, PhysioToolkit, and PhysioNet, Circulation 101(23), 2000; Moody and Mark, The impact of the MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Database, IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology 20(3), 2001.
